title: A monic relative torus homomorphism is a closed immersion
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Let $P\to S$ be a torus: a smooth affine commutative $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] which is fppf locally isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ for finite locally constant rank $r\geq0$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $G\to S$ be a separated $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $u:P\to G$ be an $S$-group homomorphism. Suppose that for every $S$-scheme $T$, the map $P(T)\to G(T)$ induced by $u$ is injective, where $P(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,P)$ and likewise for $G$. Then $u$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem 5.3.5 and direct proof, printed pp.165–168, specialized to a torus. For the nonaffine target reduction the proof offers Prasad–Yu, Proposition 3.1, as the Raynaud affineness input; no SGA source is used. Original not archived locally.

proof.text: The hypothesis on $T$-points makes $u$ a monomorphism of schemes. Indeed, if $a,b:Z\to P$ satisfy $ua=ub$, their composites to $S$ agree, so give one $S$-scheme structure on $Z$; injectivity on $P(Z)$ then gives $a=b$. The same argument, or the fibre-product universal property, shows monicity after every base change.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.5, proof, p.166: monicity and base change; explicit Yoneda argument.

proof.text: Choose the fppf splitting covering for $P$, refining its members by affine opens on which the rank is constant. Its pullback to $G$ is an fppf covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], hence an fpqc covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. The morphisms obtained from $u$ are its base changes to that covering of its target. By [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion], it suffices to prove closedness on these pieces. Thus assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $P=\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$ with a fixed finite $r$, including $r=0$.

Use the affine Noetherian approximation [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], with $A$ the directed union of its finite-type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $A_i$. By [thm-pd-spreading-out], descend $G$ as a finitely presented scheme to some $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$; take $P_i=\mathbf G_{m,A_i}^r$. The products needed for group laws are the products of these models. The same theorem descends multiplication, identity, inverse, and $u$ to a common stage. Its equality clause makes the finitely many associativity, unit, inverse and homomorphism diagrams commute at a later stage. Explicitly these diagrams have domains among $S_i,G_i,G_i^2,G_i^3,P_i,P_i^2$, with products over $S_i$; their arrows are identities, projections, the descended operations and $u_i$. Thus they give an actual group scheme and group homomorphism, whose base change recovers the given operations and $u$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), parts (1)–(3); Conrad Theorem 5.3.5, p.166, direct-limit reduction.

proof.text: Enlarge the stage so that $G_i\to S_i$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-separated], and $u_i$ is a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-monomorphism]. The latter requires local finite type at the starting stage: on affine opens of $P_i$ mapping into an affine open of $G_i$, finite generators over $A_i$ also generate over the target coordinate algebra, so this hypothesis holds. All the schemes in these descent applications are qcqs, being finitely presented over affine $S_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $S_i,G_i,P_i$ are Noetherian, since they are of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. In particular $u_i$ is quasi-compact (every open in its Noetherian source is quasi-compact), so the local finite-type assertion makes $u_i$ finite type. Fix this stage and write $S_0,P_0,G_0,u_0$.

It suffices to show $u_0$ proper, since [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] then makes this monomorphism a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-dvr-properness] to the finite-type morphism $u_0:P_0\to G_0$, whose target is Noetherian by step 4. Fix an arbitrary DVR $R$ with fraction field $K$, a point $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to G_0$, and $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to P_0$ with $u_0a=b|_K$. Pull back the group schemes along the composite $\operatorname{Spec}R\to G_0\to S_0$; denote them $P_R,G_R$ and the homomorphism $u_R$. We will prove $u_R$ is closed and explicitly extend this square. No finiteness or excellence assumption on $R$ is added.

The generic map $u_K:P_K\to G_K$ is a closed immersion by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-monomorphism-closed-immersion]: both groups are separated of finite type over $K$, and step 1 gives injectivity on all algebra points. Let $C\hookrightarrow G_R$ be the schematic closure of this closed subgroup supplied by [lem-sfb-dvr-flat-generic-subgroup-closure]. It is separated, flat and finitely presented over $R$, and $C_K=u_K(P_K)$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-character-reconstruction] to the constant lattice sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z^r}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$: it identifies its constructed smooth torus with $P_R=\mathbf G_{m,R}^r$. Hence $P_R$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The flat-source factorization clause of the closure node therefore gives $v:P_R\to C$ with composite $u_R$. Its compatibility with the group operations follows by composing the required equalities with the monomorphism $C\hookrightarrow G_R$. Likewise $v$ is monic since $u_R$ is monic.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.5, proof, p.166, generic-image schematic closure and factorization; field input from Milne Proposition 5.31(a), Theorem 5.34.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-generic-affine-group-affine] to $C$. Its flatness, separatedness and finite type were supplied in step 6. Its generic fibre is the split torus $P_K$, hence affine. Thus $C$ is affine over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. This is the point that handles a possibly nonaffine original target $G_R$.

source.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.1, PDF p.5; affineness input explicitly offered in Conrad Theorem 5.3.5, p.166.

proof.text: The torus $P_R$ is of multiplicative type with character group $\mathbf Z^r$: its coordinate algebra is $R[\mathbf Z^r]=R[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ with the stated diagonal comultiplication. Thus [lem-sfb-affine-multiplicative-type-monomorphism-closed] applies to the monic group homomorphism $v:P_R\to C$, with affine finitely presented target $C$ by steps 6–7. It makes $v$ a closed immersion. Composing with $C\hookrightarrow G_R$ gives a closed immersion $u_R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp].

source.place: Appendix B, Lemma B.1.3, pp.281–282, after Theorem 5.3.5 nonaffine-target reduction; morphisms.tex Tag 01QS (lemma-composition-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Extend the square of step 5 directly. The point $b$ gives a section $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}R\to G_R$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing its closed-point image. Its inverse image under $\beta$ contains the closed point of the local scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence is all of it. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $u_R^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ for an ideal $I$. The ring map $B\to R$ of $\beta$ carries $I$ to zero in $K$, because its generic restriction factors through $P_K$ by $a$. Since $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, it kills $I$ already in $R$, and so defines a map $B/I\to R$. This gives the desired lift to $P_R$, hence to $P_0$; its restriction is $a$ and its uniqueness follows from monicity. Every square therefore has a unique lift. The criterion [lem-sfb-noetherian-dvr-properness] proves $u_0$ proper, and [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] proves it closed.

source.place: Tag 0208 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper), (3) implies (1); affine factorization written out using Morphisms Tag 01QO; etale.tex Tag 04XV.

proof.text: Base change of $u_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S_0$ recovers $u$ on the split affine piece, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes it a closed immersion. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to the target covering in step 2. This proves the assertion for the original $S,P,G,u$.
